story.name: トウキョウ ひとりぐらし
story.title: A Small Room by the River
story.line: ブーケが トウキョウで ひとりぐらしを はじめます
story.ja: 8月の最後の夜、オハイオの小さな町から来たブーケが、中目黒の目黒川ぞいの小さなアパートに着く。はじめてのひとり暮らし。大家のたぬきちが部屋を案内し、ごみの日（燃えるごみは火・金、プラは水、缶・びんは隔週の木曜）を説明する。真下の部屋のアリゲッティが声をかけてくれて「何かあったらノックしてね」。荷ほどきするつもりが、ブーケは服のまま、夜10時前に眠ってしまう。

segments.en: On the last night of August, a little train pulled into Nakameguro Station, and Rosie stepped off it with two big suitcases.
She also had a backpack that was much too full, a map on her phone, and a key she had never used.
Two weeks ago, she was living in a small town in Ohio. Now she had a job in Tokyo, and an apartment of her own.
It was her first time living alone. Her mom had cried at the airport. Rosie had cried a little on the plane, too.
The air was hot and heavy, even at nine at night. The cicadas were still buzzing in the trees, like somebody had left a radio on.
She rolled her suitcases along a narrow street by the Meguro River. The water was low and quiet, and cherry trees leaned over it from both sides.
Okay. Left at the bakery, then right at the vending machine. Wait. There's a vending machine on every corner. This could take a while.
Her building was small and white, just two floors, with stairs on the outside and a row of potted plants by the front door.
The landlord, Tom Nook, was waiting under the light with a folder, smiling like he had been waiting all day.
Welcome, welcome! You must be Rosie. How was your flight? Long, I'm sure. Come in, come in. Shoes off right here, please.
The apartment was one room, six tatami mats, with a tiny kitchen, a tiny bathroom, and a sliding glass door to a tiny balcony.
Everything was small and clean, and it all fit together like a puzzle. Rosie loved it right away.
Now, this is very important. The trash schedule. Burnable trash on Tuesdays and Fridays. Plastic on Wednesdays. Cans and bottles every other Thursday.
Every other Thursday. Okay. I'm going to need to write this down. Actually, can I just take a picture of it?
Of course, of course. It's a lot to take in on your first night. Don't worry. You'll get the hang of it. Everybody does.
He showed her how the hot water worked, which buttons on the toilet did what, and where to leave her shoes. Then he handed her the folder.
Make yourself at home, Rosie. And if you need anything at all, my number's on the first page. Good night!
And then he was gone, and it was very, very quiet.
Rosie sat down in the middle of her new room. There was no furniture yet. Just her suitcases, the folder, and the hum of the fridge.
Hi, apartment. I'm Rosie. I guess we live together now. I promise I'll learn the trash schedule.
She opened the glass door and stepped out onto the balcony. From there, she could see a little piece of the river, and the city lights beyond it.
Somewhere down the street, a train went by. Somewhere else, a dog barked twice, and then thought better of it.
Then a door opened downstairs, and a voice called up to her, soft and friendly.
Hello? Are you the new neighbor? I heard the suitcases on the stairs. I'm Gayle. I live right below you.
Gayle was an older lady with reading glasses on a chain, and she was holding a watering can, even though it was dark.
Hi! Yes, I'm Rosie. I just got here. Sorry about the noise. Those suitcases weigh about as much as I do.
Oh, don't worry about it, dear. I lived in California for ten years when I was young. I remember my first night there.
Get some sleep. Tomorrow, everything will feel a little less strange. And come knock if you need anything.
Rosie thanked her and went back inside. She meant to unpack. She meant to take a shower. She meant to call her mom.
Instead, she lay down on the tatami for just a minute, still in her clothes, and she was out like a light.
It wasn't even ten o'clock. Outside, the cicadas finally stopped, and the river kept going, slow and dark, under the cherry trees.

ph.trap: every other＝ほかの全部 ではなく「ひとつおき」

ph.ja: いっぺんには覚えきれない
ph.trap: take in＝中に入れる ではなく、情報を受けとめる
hang＝つるす ではなく「やり方の感じ」

ph.ja: 自分の家だと思ってくつろいでね
ph.trap: 家を作る ではなく、くつろいでという決まり文句

ph.ja: 何かあったら（言ってね）
ph.trap: 本当に困ったら頼っていいという、温かい申し出
もっとよく考えた ではなく、考えなおしてやめた
電気が消える ではなく、ぐっすり眠りこむ

predict.ask: ブーケは よなかに なにを する？
choices: She knocks on Gayle's door to borrow some food.
She wakes up at three in the morning, starving, and goes to the convenience store.
She sleeps all the way to the next evening.
predict.ja: 夜中の3時におなかぺこぺこで目がさめ、コンビニに行く。
